one_month_reasoning: Window 10/20-11/19/2026 holds: (1) Oct 28 FOMC, hold ~87% (DeFi Rate Kalshi/Polymarket) - little news; (2) Oct 29 Q3 results with the first 2027 guidance and the rolled-forward 2027-2031 capital and financing plan (Business Wire). Base rate: XEL has met or beaten guidance 21 years running, and plan roll-forwards usually raise capex; the risk is a bigger equity need with the stock near 17x. Consensus Q3 EPS $1.37 drifted up in the last week. I expect 2027 guidance bracketing ~$4.50-4.60 (rate-base build $4.55), which is roughly priced; (3) Nov 3 midterms, where affordability and data-center politics are live in MN/CO; (4) a likely Anthropic IPO (Polymarket: November 62%, by Nov 30 65%), whose index and fund flows fall mainly on AI/tech holders, not regulated utilities (Wellington on same-sector rebalancing); (5) MPUC Minnesota gas-case decision expected November. The biggest short-run driver is the 10Y (5.12%, down from 5.31% on 10/5; Polymarket has 23.5% on <5.00% in October). After the +9% rally off the 9/24 low ($68.72) I take no momentum or reversal view: median ~$76.9, sigma ~5.7% (19% annual vol / 3.5 plus a little for the earnings and plan event), slightly fatter left tail for a plan or equity surprise.

fair_value.method: Rate-base EPS build ($4.55 2027, $5.06 2028; NTM at the horizon $4.95) x 16.9x NTM P/E (0.9x the 18.85x peer median) = $83.66, weight 0.8; driver FCFF DCF (7.0% WACC, 14.0x exit EBITDA, net debt $50.4B and 650M shares at the horizon) weight 0.2; blended engine base value $79.11.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM EPS at 2027-10-20 $4.95 (rate-base build: avg rate base x 54-54.5% equity x 8.45-8.55% earned ROE - holdco drag, / 645-672M shares) x 16.9x (peer median 18.85x x ~0.9 current relative)

inputs_detail.derivation: Rate-base build: EPS = (avg rate base x equity ratio x earned ROE - holdco/financing drag)/avg shares. 2026: (56+66)/2=61B x 54% x 8.45% = 2,783 - 220 = 2,563 / 625M = $4.10 (guidance midpoint $4.04-4.16). 2027: 71.5B x 54% x 8.45% = 3,263 - 330 = 2,933 / 645M = $4.55 (consensus $4.54). 2028: 81.5B x 54.5% x 8.55% = 3,798 - 400 = 3,398 / 672M = $5.06 (Gabelli/FactSet $5.03). NTM at 10/20/2027 = 0.2 x 4.55 + 0.8 x 5.06 = $4.96 -> $4.95. Earned ROE 8.45% = TTM ongoing total-opco ROE 8.43% (Q2 deck slide 25), below allowed 9.3-9.6% (regulatory lag, PSCo 7.22%).
inputs_detail.variant_view: If PSCo lag closes after the 2026 Colorado electric settlement (ROE 9.3%) earned ROE could reach 8.8% -> 2028 EPS ~$5.25 (+$3/share at 16.9x); if lag widens with higher rates, 8.2% -> ~$4.85 (-$3.5).

inputs_detail.derivation: Peer median NTM P/E 18.85x (12 peers, range 17.1-21.5x). XEL now 76.68 / (0.2 x 4.12 + 0.8 x 4.54 = 4.46) = 17.2x = 0.91x the median. Hold the relative (~0.90 x 18.85 = 16.97) and the group level (already reflects 10Y at 5.1%), round down to 16.9x. The persistent discount reflects wildfire liability (Smokehouse Creek, Texas AG suit), PSCo lag and the $7B equity need; it is below XEL's 5-yr forward average 19.8x (Seeking Alpha) and 10-yr ~19.5x (Sure Dividend), which were set when the 10Y was 1.5-4%.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Re-rating to the peer median (18.85x) adds ~$9.7/share; a rates shock to 14.5x subtracts ~$12.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: FCFF FY2026-30 on revenue $15.6B->$20.6B, GAAP EBIT margin 19-22%, D&A ~20-21% of revenue, capex $13.8/16.1/14.2/10.5/10.4B; WACC 7.0%; exit 14.0x FY2030 EBITDA; net debt at horizon $50.4B; 650M shares

inputs_detail.derivation: 10-K FY2025 income statement 'Total operating revenues 14,669' (XBRL revenue not in the fact pack; read from the filing).

GAAP operating income FY2025 $2,583M on $14,669M = 17.6%; TTM to 6/2026 $2,789M (F6). Margin expands as return on a faster-growing rate base outpaces pass-through revenue. GAAP operating income excludes AFUDC-equity and other income (~$855M TTM = F81 2,002 - F6 2,789 + F67 1,642), so the engine's NOPAT-minus-interest EPS sits below the build; see structure_note.

Effective rate FY2025 = -245/1,773 = -13.8%; TTM = -231/2,002 = -11.5% (production tax credits, transferred for cash). Set slightly less negative and drifting up as credit-eligible additions end after the 2027 phase-out window.

inputs_detail.derivation: Base plan $13,790 / 15,130 / 12,650 / 9,020 / 9,410M (Q2 deck slide 28) plus 50% of the $10B+ line-of-sight incremental capital, spread 0 / 1.0 / 1.5 / 1.5 / 1.0B (judgment on approvals: SPS ~2,600 MW recommended, PSCo ~800 MW approved, NSP Google-funded generation pending).

inputs_detail.derivation: Cost of equity 8.4% = 10Y 5.12% (Treasury 10/20/2026) + beta ~0.6 x ERP 5.5% (low-beta regulated utility, judgment), cross-checked against authorized electric ROE avg 9.84% (Gabelli/RRA 1H26). Pre-tax cost of debt ~5.4% (2026 issues 4.15%-5.875%, Q2 deck), after-tax ~5.1% given ~5% effective tax. Weights: equity 624.6M x $76.68 = $47.9B; net debt $37.4B (F91) -> 56/44. 0.56 x 8.4% + 0.44 x 5.1% = 6.97%.

inputs_detail.value: exit EV/EBITDA 14.0x on FY2030 GAAP EBITDA
inputs_detail.derivation: Exit at end-2030 is a trailing multiple: peer TTM EV/EBITDA median ~13.3x (AEP 13.7, DUK 10.8, SO 13.0, ETR 14.5, WEC 15.1, CMS 13.3, AEE 13.3, LNT 15.4, CNP 12.8, EVRG 12.6, NEE 17.6); XEL's own TTM = (47.9 + 37.4)/5.72 = 14.9x (F92). 14.0x sits between, since GAAP EBITDA excludes XEL's large AFUDC. Gordon not used: 2030 FCFF is still negative in the build-out.
inputs_detail.variant_view: At XEL's own 14.9x the DCF rises ~$7/share; at the 13.3x peer median it falls ~$5.

inputs_detail.derivation: 37,447 + capex H2-2026 7,820 (13,790 plan - 5,970 YTD) + Jan-Oct 2027 12,900 (0.8 x 16,130) - CFO net of dividends ~4.4B/yr x 1.31 yr = 5,800 (between TTM CFO-dividends 4,771-1,365 = 3.4B and the plan average 30,180/5 = 6.0B) - equity settled ~1,900 = 50,467 -> 50,400.
624.6M outstanding 7/28/2026 + ~$1.9B of the $7B 2026-30 equity plan (85% contracted via forwards) settled by Oct-2027 at ~$75 = ~25M -> ~650M. (650/624.6)^(1/1.23)-1 = 3.3%/yr.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Q3 plan update (Oct 29) may raise the equity need with a larger capital plan (+40% equity on incremental capex): +10M shares = -1.5% EPS.

comps_summary.peer_range: NTM P/E 17.1x (CMS) to 21.5x (ETR); NTM EV/EBITDA 9.6x (DUK) to 11.7x (NEE) for the 5 peers with EBITDA consensus; EPS growth +6.9% to +18.3%
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 16.9x NTM at the horizon vs 18.85x median: ~10% discount, the same relative as today (XEL 17.2x on the 0.2/0.8 FY26/FY27 blend of $4.46).
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: XEL's 2026-28 EPS growth (~9-10%) is above the peer median (~8%), which alone would argue for a premium. The discount has held since the Feb-2024 Smokehouse Creek fire (stock -8% on the day, Business Insurance) and is backed by things that last past the horizon: (a) open wildfire tails - Smokehouse Creek $460M estimated loss plus legal costs, with penalties and government claims not estimable, and the Texas AG negligence suit (Dec 2025); Marshall Fire ~$640M settlement; a Colorado/Texas/New Mexico service area with wildfire exposure; (b) PSCo earned 7.22% vs a 9.3% settlement ROE, the widest lag in the group's large names; (c) the $7B equity need, now priced at a higher cost of capital, and the Minnesota AG's Oct-1 opposition to the Google ESA. I keep the current relative rather than close it, because sell-side 'will outperform' calls are not evidence and none of (a)-(c) resolves by Oct-2027. Before the fire XEL traded at a premium (10-yr average ~19.5x vs the group); a re-rating to the median is the bull case, not the base.

thesis_break_reason: $63 is ~14x the current NTM EPS ($4.46), ~2 turns below where the group traded at the 5.3% 10Y peak in late September (XEL bottomed at $68.72 = 15.4x then). Rates alone did not get XEL there, so a trade below $63 most likely means a fundamental break: a new wildfire liability (Colorado/Texas fire season), a sharply worse Colorado or Minnesota order (ROE cut, Google ESA rejected, large-load tariff without collateral), or a capital plan cut or equity reset that moves 2028 EPS below ~$4.80. Ordinary rate volatility should hold above the bear value ($64).

reverse_dcf_check: Engine reverse DCF: holding the 14.0x exit, the P/E leg ($83.7) needs a 4.1% WACC, so the market is not pricing XEL on regulated return = cost of capital. As a growth-perpetuity check, P/E = (1 - g/ROE)/(k - g): 16.9x fits a ~7.0% cost of equity (about the 10Y + 2pt, below my 8.4% CAPM figure) with 2.9-3.6% perpetual growth at an 8.5-9.5% earned ROE. At an 8.4% cost of equity it would need ~6.6% perpetual growth with the ROE lag fully closed (9.5%), which is too much; and with earned ROE stuck near 8.45% (about the cost of equity) the justified P/E is ~12x whatever the growth, which is what the DCF leg says. So the horizon multiple rests on the market keeping a low implied cost of equity for regulated utilities and on some of the lag closing. That is rate-sensitive, which is why the bear case is mainly a rates and regulation case. Post-horizon risks (wildfire, data-center shortfall, ROE pressure) are covered by keeping the ~10% discount to the peer median rather than closing it.

sbc_treatment.note: FY2025 share-based compensation $46M (F36), ~0.3% of revenue and ~$0.08/share. Ongoing EPS (guidance, consensus and the rate-base build) is after stock comp; the engine's EBIT is GAAP operating income after stock comp. Share count grows only by equity issuance (~3.3%/yr), not by SBC add-backs.

reasoning: Base rates first: XEL's 12-month price returns over 2005-2026 (250 overlapping windows, Twelve Data) had median +8.3%, s.d. 12.6%, 26% negative, 10% below -10%; after a negative prior year the median was +10%. That record was built mostly in a falling-rate era, and the current setup is the opposite: 10Y 5.12% (5.31% on 10/5, highest since 2002 per Gabelli), a Fed that hiked on 9/16, and prediction markets pricing another hike (Polymarket Dec +25bp 77.5%, 10Y >= 5.5% before 2027 25%). Utilities fell 13% in Q3-2026 on rates, not fundamentals (Gabelli); the sector trailing P/E is still at the 78th percentile since 1979 (Siblis). So I center a little below the historical drift: rate-base EPS growth (~11% NTM to NTM, $4.46 -> $4.95) roughly offsets a hold-the-relative multiple of 16.9x and DCF drag, giving a horizon value of $79.1 (+3% price, ~+6% with the ~3% dividend). The scenario mix (25% bear $64 on rates/regulation/wildfire, 50% base $79, 25% bull $89) with 11% within-scenario spread gives a median ~$78 and an inter-quartile ~$69-87, about the stock's 19% realized vol; the left tail is fattened for wildfire jump risk (Feb-2024 single-day -8%). On Kilian's question: the Anthropic IPO (Polymarket ~65% by Nov 30, ~$1.5-2T) is unlikely to drain liquidity from XEL. Index and fund rebalancing pressure falls on same-sector holders (Wellington on SpaceX), and XEL's holders are income and utility funds, not the AI-growth money that will fund the IPO. A dip caused by a broad risk-off around the deal, with the 10Y and fundamentals unchanged, would be a buying opportunity below ~$70 (15.7x NTM, the late-September washout level). Below the $63 thesis break, re-underwrite instead. Fundamentally the WSJ S-1 details (~$450B of mostly noncancelable cloud commitments; Google $111B plus a >$160B TPU lease) support hyperscaler capacity demand, and Google is XEL's ~1 GW Pine Island customer. But I found no named source tying Anthropic workloads to any XEL-served site; its reported Texas sites (Rockdale, Bastrop) are in Central Texas, outside SPS's Panhandle/South Plains territory, so this is a general demand signal only. The S-1's warning that data-center opposition is 'more organized and coordinated' is already visible in XEL's states: the MN AG opposes the Google ESA as filed. Counterparty risk from AI tenants sits mainly with the large-load tariffs (MN: 15-yr minimum, 80% demand-charge exit fee; CO: deposits and study fees; Google ESA credit protections), so for shareholders it is a growth risk more than a balance-sheet risk. Research was limited to public pages; X/Twitter was not used.

model_inputs.structure_note: Regulated utility: value is carried by the rate-base earnings build priced on forward P/E (weight 0.8) with a driver FCFF DCF at 0.2 (forward P/E 17.2x on the run date falls in the 15.0-19.6x band). EPS = avg rate base ($61B 2026, $71.5B 2027, $81.5B 2028 from the $56/66/77/86B base-plan path) x equity ratio 54-54.5% x earned ROE 8.45-8.55% less holdco/financing drag ($220M/$330M/$400M), over avg shares 625/645/672M -> $4.10/$4.55/$5.06, within 1% of guidance midpoint and consensus. The P/E leg uses that stated EPS. The engine's own NOPAT-minus-interest EPS is far lower because GAAP operating income excludes AFUDC-equity and other income (~$855M TTM) and the engine charges interest on all net debt with no AFUDC-debt credit; the EBIT margins are kept on the GAAP operating-income basis so the DCF's cash flows are right, rather than forced to match EPS. No SOTP: segment (opco) EPS is not reported in a way that gives separate multiples, and all four opcos are vertically integrated electric/gas utilities priced the same way.
model_inputs.gap_note: fair_value.value equals the engine's base horizon value.

model_inputs.dcf_check: Engine DCF $60.95/share vs P/E leg $83.66 (-27%). Why: (1) the FCFF DCF counts 2027-2030 capex of ~$51B as cash out while much of the asset base it builds is still in construction (earning AFUDC, not cash) at the 2030 exit, and the exit multiple is applied to GAAP EBITDA that excludes AFUDC; (2) at a 14.0x exit on a 7.0% WACC the regulated return is roughly the cost of capital, so the DCF values the equity near book-plus-a-little, while the market prices the group at ~2x book on the spread between allowed ROE (~9.8%) and a lower implied cost of equity. The engine's reverse DCF says the multiples need a ~4.1% WACC at a 14.0x exit, or equivalently a ~16x exit at 7%. The DCF keeps its 0.2 weight (P/E-band rule); it is the honest 'no ROE-over-COE premium' anchor and pulls the blend about $4.5 below the P/E leg.
